calls.head: Look for Montréal to find the slot
calls.body: Montréal’s shots are among the league’s most dangerous (1st of 32: one expected goal for every 14.5 unblocked shots). Carolina ranks 32nd at keeping opponents to the outside.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: Montréal needed 15.5 unblocked shots per expected goal, against its usual 14.5.

calls.head: Montréal can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: Carolina ranks 6th of 32 on the power play (8.1 expected goals per 60); Montréal ranks 26th on the penalty kill.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: Carolina’s power play created 4.3 expected goals per 60 in 6:11 of 5-on-4 time, against its usual 8.1, and scored 1 goal.

calls.head: Two of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams
calls.body: Carolina’s hit score is 109 (7th of 32) and Montréal’s is 107 (10th). 100 is league average, after adjusting for each arena’s scorer.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: The two teams’ combined hit score was 140, against their usual 108 (100 is league average, after adjusting for the arena’s scorer).

surprises.head: Carolina shot far more than usual
surprises.body: 83.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5, adjusted for score and venue, against its usual 65.8.

surprises.head: Montréal shot far less than usual
surprises.body: 30.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5, adjusted for score and venue, against its usual 55.7.

surprises.head: Montréal tried a different line
surprises.body: A. Newhook, J. Slafkovský, K. Dach played 5:00 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Montréal’s usual lines.
